description: Held-out cases for lesson 15. Never used while iterating on a prompt - only to check that an improvement generalised rather than being fitted to the training set.

cases.input: The invoice for October says 12 seats but we only have 9. Can you re-issue it? Finance needs it for the month-end close, which is a fortnight away.
URGENT!!! Please please add dark mode. I stare at this all day and it's blinding. Take your time though.
Signing in redirects me back to the login page forever. Started after your update. Two of us can't work.
I placed an order last week and I'd like to know roughly when it leaves the warehouse. No rush.

labelling_rule: Urgency labels follow one decidable rule, applied first-match-wins: HIGH if money is actively at risk, more than one person is blocked right now, or a deadline within 24 hours is stated. LOW if the writer says there is no rush, or states no deadline and describes no blockage. MEDIUM otherwise. The word 'URGENT' is not evidence by itself. If you disagree with a label, the rule is what to argue with - a gold label you cannot defend from a written rule is noise, not ground truth.
